title: Fang Bo pulls out of WTT Star Contender Muscat and goes home for treatment on a serious injury
seo_title: Fang Bo quits WTT Star Contender Muscat to treat injury
description: Fang Bo says his injury is serious after two injections and he is going home for treatment, two days after winning WTT Contender Istanbul for Kazakhstan.
standfirst: The 34-year-old had planned five WTT events in a row, but said after his first match in Oman that carrying on could cause a very serious problem.
body: Fang Bo has pulled out of WTT Star Contender Muscat and is going home for treatment, saying his injury is serious and that playing on risked a very serious problem, two days after he won WTT Contender Istanbul.

The 34-year-old, who now plays for Kazakhstan, withdrew from the men's singles before his second qualifying match on Tuesday, giving Romania's Eduard Ionescu a walkover. He also missed the mixed doubles, where he had been due to play with Austria's Sofia Polcanova.

Fang explained his decision in a social media post on Tuesday, reported by Xinhua and The Paper. He said he had planned to play five WTT events in a row and had prepared a great deal for them, and that he had had two injections to manage the injury.

"At the first event, the injection didn't work very well. At the second, although I won the title, the injury was still fairly serious," Fang wrote (translated from Chinese). "I wanted to do my best to see this Star Contender through too, but after my first match I felt that if I kept going a very serious problem might occur."

He said he had decided to give up the rest of the event and go home for treatment so that he could compete better later on. He did not say what the injury was. His courtside coach in Istanbul, Li Liangfu, had said Fang played that tournament with a neck injury and needed treatment and painkillers before every match.
Before Istanbul, Fang played the WTT Feeder in Vila Nova de Gaia in Portugal earlier this month, where he lost in the last 32 of the singles.

Fang was part of the China team that won the 2016 World Team Championships and reached the men's singles final at the 2015 World Championships in Suzhou, where he lost to Ma Long. He retired from the national team in 2021 and returned in April this year playing for Kazakhstan, under terms that keep him out of the Olympics, the World Championships and the World Cup.

In Istanbul he entered as a wild card ranked 160th and won his first international singles title since 2013, beating South Korea's Kang Dongsoo 4-1 in the final, as Eleven [reported on Sunday](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-finals-fang-bo-honoka-hashimoto-titles.html). The title lifted him 94 places to 66th in Monday's world ranking.

He flew straight on to Oman and [came from a game down](/news/wtt-star-contender-muscat-2026-qualifying-day-one-fang-bo-yigenler.html) to beat Turkey's Abdullah Yigenler 9-11, 11-6, 11-8, 11-9 in the first qualifying round on Monday. Chinese accounts of that match said he looked weary in the opening two games.

Fang and Polcanova, the seventh seeds in mixed doubles qualifying, were replaced in the draw by South Korea's Ma Yeongmin and Kim Seongjin, who lost 11-8, 11-3, 11-9 to China's Yuan Licen and Wang Xiaotong.

Ionescu, the world No 81 and third seed in men's qualifying, plays Russia's Maksim Grebnev, a 3-0 winner over Australia's Aditya Sareen in the second round, for a main-draw place on Tuesday afternoon. The main draw starts on Wednesday, with Darko Jorgic, Shunsuke Togami and Dang Qiu the top three seeds in the men's singles.
Fang has not said when he expects to play again.
